We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need to produce JSON route with 3 reactions. Steps forward: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). 3) Doebner modification to create α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid.

Thus retrosynthetic steps: target -> break amide bond to give acid (aryl-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid?) and aniline (the first aromatic ring with sulfonamide). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid (or maybe the unsaturated acid is from Doebner). Actually the target contains /C=C/C(=O)N- attached to aromatic ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The unsaturated amide side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. The Doebner modification would give the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2. Then amide formation attaches the aniline to that acid. So retrosynthesis: target -> break amide to give α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride attached to first aromatic ring (with methyl) and aniline (the second aromatic ring? Actually sulfonamide is between first aromatic ring (with methyl) and sulfonyl group attached to second aromatic ring). The sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to first ring. So break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2) and aniline (the first ring with methyl). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). That matches Doebner.

Thus we need templates for each step. We need to find template IDs for these transformations. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with appropriate functional groups.

Step 1: amide formation (forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). Functional groups broken: carboxylic acid (aliphatic? but here it's aromatic carboxylic acid). Use "aromatic carboxylic acid". Formed: amide. So search.
